line:
I climb to my old bed, set the greataxe against the wall with Dargan's sash hanging straight, and lie still for a moment holding the horn charm in my fist. "Father, tomorrow I stand beside a man who once took your pass, for the sake of his men and his ninety-four hands, so keep a watch over me and don't let me get loud when I should be quiet."

Then I sleep, soundly, so that by dawn I'm rested and level-headed for the hearing at the Stones.

entries.text: time: 10 hours 30 minutes later: Day 30, 6:30:12 AM

You lie in the dark with Dargan's horn charm in your fist and say it low, so as not to wake the house: keep a watch over me tomorrow, and don't let me get loud when I should be quiet. The rafters creak. Downstairs Pip mutters a number in his sleep. You sleep, and nobody counts you.

You wake before the cock, rested and clear-headed. Veshra has porridge on the hob and says nothing about the hour. Tessa comes down dressed, pale, with the knotted cord wound round her wrist. You walk to the Stones together through new snow, the three of you and Pip a pace behind, and Wren on your shoulders until she is told to get down and be solemn.

The hearing is already gathering when you arrive. Harrowmere has come in its shawls and boots, hundreds of them, ranged in a rough ring on the trampled snow around the three weathered stones. Hale Orrin stands at the front with his staff. The man whose nephew died at Cinder Ford is near him, grey-faced, with his arms folded. Forty Tallies stand on the far side with their helms off and their spears left stacked behind them, and Dreg is at their head. Ushk stands a little apart, his hands open at his sides. Between the stones, two Tally guards bring Brakk forward with his arm in its splint. He walks on his own feet, his face closed, his eyes moving over the crowd as if counting it.

Gorrak waits at the middle stone, bareheaded, the burn livid in the cold light. He looks at you once and nods. It's a little after half past six on Day 30, the sun just lifting over the eastern fields.

Veshra goes into the ring leaning on her stick, and the noise falls away. She stops before the stones and turns slowly, until she faces Brakk. "I am Dargan's sister," she says. "I will ask once."

All of Harrowmere is silent. Tessa has found your sleeve. Gorrak stands to your left, and you have promised to hold your tongue.

What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

features: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

Breath Weapon: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor: - You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. - When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table. - You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. At level 2: rage damage bonus +2; 2 rages before a long rest.
Unarmored Defense: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

Reckless Attack: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Danger Sense: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 30 ~7 AM, the hearing at the Border Stones: asked by Veshra who struck Dargan and how, Brakk deflected and said 'Ask your captain who gave the order,' trying to put the killing on Gorrak Vael. Whether Gorrak gave any such order is for play to settle; Gorrak did say on Day 25 that he did not know Dargan was struck from behind.

entries.text:
You set the greataxe against the wall with Dargan's sash hanging straight, lie back, and hold the horn charm in your fist. You ask your father to keep a watch over you tomorrow, and not to let you get loud when you should be quiet. The rafters creak. Somewhere below, Pip's snore stops and starts again. You sleep soundly.

You wake in grey light with a clear head. Veshra has laid out porridge and your cleaned cloak. Tessa says nothing over breakfast, but she tucks the knotted cord inside her sleeve and walks beside you all the way to the Stones.

The whole town is there. Herders stand in shawls and sheepskins in a great ring around the three weathered stones, with the lamp-woman at the front and the man who lost his nephew at Cinder Ford, grim and silent. Hale Orrin leans on his staff beside Veshra, who sits on a folding stool in the middle of the ring, small and straight-backed. Dreg's Tallies stand on the far side with their helms off, unarmed. Ushk is among them. Gorrak stands apart with his burned face bare to the cold.

Dreg's men bring Brakk out between two guards, his arm in its splint. His eyes sweep the ring once, settle on Veshra, and stay there.

It is a little after seven in the morning. Veshra lifts her stick and the murmur dies. She looks at Brakk for a long moment.

"You were at the Goat's Throat the day my brother died," she says. "I will ask you once, in front of everyone who loved him. Who struck Dargan down, and how?"

Brakk's face doesn't change. He looks, very briefly, at Gorrak.

"Ask your captain," he says. "Ask him who gave the order."

The ring draws a breath. Gorrak doesn't move. Tessa's hand finds your sleeve. You promised to stand at Gorrak's shoulder and keep your mouth shut unless someone put a blade or a lie in the way.

What does Korvash do?

input.add_to_description: Day 30 ~7 AM: the hearing of Brakk begins at the Border Stones before the town of Harrowmere (one side) and forty Tallies with spears stacked (the other). Veshra stands before the stones with her stick, ready to put the question to Brakk as Dargan's sister.

entries.text:
You climb to your old bed, stand the greataxe against the wall with Dargan's sash hanging straight, and lie holding the horn charm in your fist. You tell your father what tomorrow holds. You will stand beside a man who once took his pass, for the sake of his men and the ninety-four hands, and you ask him to keep watch over you and not let you be loud when you should be quiet.

The house answers with its small noises: a settling beam, Wren muttering in her sleep, the hearth ticking down. The charm is warm from your hand. You sleep soundly, and nothing wakes you.

Veshra's hand on your shoulder does. It is half past six on Day 30, and the window is a pale grey square. "Up," she says. "The town is walking." She has put porridge on the table and has her best clan shawl pinned at the throat. Tessa is already dressed, with the knotted cord wound at her wrist. Pip has combed his hair flat with water and looks as if he is going to be judged himself.

Outside, the snow is trodden into a long dark line along the high road. Harrowmere is going to the Stones in twos and threes: herders with crooks, women with children by the hand, Hale Orrin in his drover's coat with his staff, and the man whose nephew died at Cinder Ford, walking alone and not looking at anyone. Nobody is talking much.

When you reach the three weathered stones the circle has already formed. The townsfolk stand on one side. On the other the Tallies stand with their helms off and their spears stacked, forty hobgoblins in neat ranks. Dreg is at the front. Brakk sits on a stool between two guards, pale, with his arm strapped to his chest. Ushk stands a little apart with his hands folded. Gorrak waits at the middle stone, bareheaded, and the burn on his face is livid in the cold. He looks at you once and nods.

Veshra takes her place before the stones with her stick planted. The crowd goes quiet, and the whole road waits on her.

Where does Korvash stand, and what does he do as the hearing begins?

input.add_to_description: Day 30, 6:30 AM: stood before the assembled town at the Border Stones for the hearing, arm splinted, guarded by two of Dreg's men. Aunt Veshra faces him to put the question. The man who lost a nephew at Cinder Ford stands in the front rank.

entries.text:
You set the greataxe against the wall with Dargan's sash hanging straight, lie back, and hold the horn charm in your fist. You say it low, to the rafters: tomorrow you stand beside the man who took his pass, for the sake of his men and the ninety-four hands, and your father is to keep watch and not let you get loud when you should be quiet.

The rafters say nothing. But the house is warm, and the snow has stopped, and you sleep as you did the night before, deep and dreamless.

You wake to a grey dawn and Tessa's knuckles on the doorframe. Veshra has porridge on the table and doesn't speak while you eat. She has put on her best clan shawl, the one with the red border that you haven't seen since you were a boy. Wren is scrubbed and solemn, and Pip has ink on his fingers again, because he insisted on bringing a slate to "write down what's said fairly."

The walk to the Stones takes an hour in the cold, with half of Harrowmere strung along the road ahead and behind you, herders, carters, and women with babies on their hips. By half past six the three stones stand in a ring of people, hundreds deep, with a clear space in the middle. Hale Orrin leans on his staff at the front. The Tallies stand on the far side without spears, helms off, in a tight quiet block with Dreg and Ushk at its head. Gorrak waits at the middle stone, bare-faced, his burn livid in the cold. Two of Dreg's men bring Brakk out of the lean-to, his arm in its splints, and stand him before the crowd. He looks at no one.

The man whose nephew died at Cinder Ford is in the front rank, with his jaw set and a woman's hand on his arm.

Veshra walks into the cleared space, leaning on her stick, and stops before Brakk. The crowd falls silent. She looks up at him a long moment. Then she looks across the circle to you, and tilts her head very slightly. Tessa has taken her place where she asked to be, and her eyes are on you.

Your place is at Gorrak's shoulder, as you promised. It's half past six in the morning, and the hearing is about to begin. What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

features: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

Breath Weapon: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation. When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
Damage Resistance: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
Draconic Ancestry (Red): breath weapon 15 ft cone, DEX save DC 12, 2d6 Fire damage (half on a success); resistance to that damage type

Rage: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor: - You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. - When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table. - You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again. At level 2: rage damage bonus +2; 2 rages before a long rest.
Unarmored Defense: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

Reckless Attack: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Danger Sense: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.
